title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: schoolmen — four conditions for certainty of obtaining; praying for another does not always obtain; Major fails that requires certain faith prayers will profit others
pass_a_gloss: This is commonly known in the School of Theologians, who are wont to say that four conditions are required that someone's prayer may have certainty of obtaining, of which one is that one pray for himself. For although it be pious, persevering, and of things pertaining unto salvation, yet if it be made for another, prayer does not always obtain. The Major proposition therefore, as you see, totters, which falsely supposes that prayers cannot rightly be made for others unless certain faith be present that they will be profitable unto the same. Nor can our doctrine of reprobation be thence refuted, that it being posited it follows that public prayers cannot be offered unto God with faith that they would profit all hearing the word of God.
pass_b_english: This is common knowledge in the School of Theologians. They say four conditions are required for a prayer to have certainty of obtaining; one is that one pray for oneself. For though the prayer be pious, persevering, and about things that belong to salvation, yet if it is made for another it does not always obtain. So the Major totters: it falsely assumes prayers cannot rightly be made for others unless certain faith is present that they will profit them. Nor is our doctrine of reprobation refuted by saying that, once posited, public prayers cannot be offered to God with faith that they would profit all who hear the Word.
source_text: Vulgo hoc notum est in Schola Theologorum, qui dicere solent, quatuor conditiones requiri ut oratio alicujus habeat certitudinem impetrandi, quarum una est, ut pro se quis oret. Nam licet sit pia, perseverans, et de pertinentibus ad salutem, tamen si pro alio fiat non semper impetrat oratio. Major itaque propositio, uti videtis, labascit, quae falso supponit preces recte fieri non posse pro aliis, nisi adsit certa fides, quod sint iisdem profuturae. Nec potest nostra de reprobatione doctrina inde refutari, quod ea posita sequatur publicas preces non posse Deo offerri cum fide quod prodessent omnibus verbum Dei audientibus.
